name: Pigmented Villonodular Synovitis

criteria.description: Chronic monoarticular joint swelling and pain
MRI showing synovial hypertrophy with low signal intensity on T2-weighted images due to hemosiderin deposition
Synovial biopsy demonstrating villous or nodular proliferation with hemosiderin-laden macrophages and multinucleated giant cells
Exclusion of other causes of monoarthritis such as infection or malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory imaging and histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on clinical suspicion supported by imaging and confirmed by biopsy.

searchTerms: persistent joint swelling in one area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Joint pain localized to affected joint
Limited range of motion in affected joint

common.symptomName: Mechanical symptoms such as locking or catching

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue mass adjacent to joint

searchTerms: grating or crackling sound in joints

rare.symptomName: Joint deformity due to chronic destruction
searchTerms: misshapen joint due to chronic injury

rare.symptomName: Pathological fracture adjacent to affected joint
searchTerms: bone fracture near joint without trauma
bone breaks due to disease near joint
symptoms from nerve or blood vessel pressure
tingling or numbness from nerve squeezing

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated (ESR, CRP)
Synovial fluid analysis typically shows non-inflammatory or mildly inflammatory profile
imaging: MRI: Synovial hypertrophy with low T2 signal intensity due to hemosiderin
X-ray: May show joint effusion, bone erosions in advanced cases
Ultrasound: Synovial thickening and joint effusion
genetic: CSF1 gene translocation reported in some cases
other: Histopathology: Villous or nodular synovial proliferation with hemosiderin-laden macrophages and multinucleated giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Positive rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP antibodies
Presence of multiple intra-articular cartilaginous loose bodies

redFlags: Unexplained soft tissue mass with systemic symptoms
references: De Saint Aubain Somerhausen N, et al. Pigmented villonodular synovitis: a review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2019.
Murphey MD, et al. Pigmented villonodular synovitis: radiologic-pathologic correlation. Radiographics. 2008.
van der Heijden L, et al. Pigmented villonodular synovitis: a review of 38 cases. J Bone Joint Surg Br. 2002.
